issues.title: [Feat] [AMD] diffusion: Enable residual_gate_add fast path on ROCm
issues.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On ROCm, the existing `residual_gate_add` Triton kernels embed NVIDIA PTX (`cvt.rn.bf16.f32` / `cvt.rn.f16.f32`, constraint `"=h"`). AMDGPU does not support the `h` register class, so LLVM aborts during compilation instead of raising a Python exception. The diffusion worker can therefore terminate during denoising before the eager fallback is reached.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

This PR adds a dedicated ROCm Triton fast path while preserving the existing CUDA implementation.

- CUDA keeps the existing JIT/custom-op path and NVIDIA PTX rounding helper, now named `_cuda_round16_f32`.
- ROCm uses a separate custom op and Triton kernels for flat and transposed layouts.
- The ROCm flat kernel also handles batched `[B, 1, D]` gates, including LTX-2's strided AdaLN views.
- ROCm BF16 rounding uses `round_bf16_to_fp32`.
- ROCm FP16 rounding uses opaque `v_cvt_f16_f32` inline assembly because a normal FP32 → FP16 → FP32 cast can be folded away by Triton.
- CUDA and ROCm use separate predicates and rounding helpers. Unsupported inputs continue to use the eager fallback.
- Existing residual-gate tests now dispatch to the appropriate backend, with a regression test ensuring HIP never enters the CUDA/PTX path.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

On gfx1151, the ROCm path was compared against the eager reference with exact comparison for FP16 and BF16.

Coverage includes FP16/BF16/FP32, full/row-broadcast/per-token/batched gates, transposed layouts, storage offsets, graph/compile paths, and unsupported-input fallback.



## Speed Tests

gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), ROCm 7.2.4, PyTorch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0.
Row-broadcast gate, wall-clock time per call:

| dtype | shape | eager | ROCm path | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 560.6 µs | 333.6 µs | 1.68x |
| bf16 | `[1, 4202, 3072]` | 568.8 µs | 341.6 µs | 1.67x |
| fp16 | `[1, 4096, 3072]` | 563.5 µs | 330.5 µs | 1.71x |
| fp16 | `[1, 4202, 3072]` | 572.3 µs | 339.4 µs | 1.69x |

These measurements cover the row-broadcast path only; the transposed ROCm path has not been independently profiled on AMD, so no speedup is claimed for that layout.

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Test Results

| Validation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `residual_gate_add` standalone | ROCm process aborts while compiling NVIDIA PTX | ROCm Triton path matches eager |
| Residual-gate test cases | Process terminated at the first case | All 55 ROCm residual-gate cases pass |
| Unsupported ROCm inputs | Eager fallback only | Unsupported inputs still use the eager fallback |

Only gfx1151 was validated locally. gfx942 and gfx950 remain for AMD CI.
CUDA was not run locally; its implementation was preserved unchanged.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

issues.body:
## Motivation

ROCm tensors also report `is_cuda`, but the diffusion residual fast path contains NVIDIA PTX. Upstream #42391 already merged the HIP eligibility guard and simplified the native dispatch. This PR now adds regression coverage on top of that implementation; it changes no production kernel.

## Changes

- Exercise HIP rejection and the exact eager result for FP16/BF16/FP32 with full, row, token, and transposed-row gate layouts. A sentinel fails the test if the PTX custom op is attempted.
- Run the real CUDA residual fast path for FP16/BF16 with those four layouts, including the new transposed Triton path, and compare with eager at `atol=0, rtol=0`.
- Run the Qwen Q/K norm + RoPE/KV packing regression with native kernels available and deliberately unavailable, checking exact model output, prefix-cache ownership, and CUDA graph replay.
- Preserve upstream's NVIDIA-only Qwen suite and newer LoRA-format tests. Remove references to the deleted failed-runtime cache and old packing eligibility API.

## Validation

Synced with upstream `bab04cd7913ff50d1bf1a677a2d10e5015dc4c3b`.

RTX 5090 D v2, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130: **44 passed** across the full residual-dispatch and Qwen CUDA test files. CUDA kernels, small-model forwards, prefix caches, and graph replay ran on the real GPU. HIP eligibility was simulated on that host; native AMD execution is still required from CI.

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_residual_gate_add_dispatch.py \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_cuda.py
```

issues.title: [Fix] true-on-policy: Cast Qwen2/Qwen3 dense inputs to params_dtype, not the quantized weight dtype
issues.body:
## Problem

`[1/42]` (true on-policy) made `Qwen3Attention.forward` and `Qwen2MLP.forward` cast their input to the
projection's weight dtype:

```python
if should_force_bfloat16_dense_tensor_math() or hidden_states.dtype != self.qkv_proj.weight.dtype:
    hidden_states = hidden_states.to(self.qkv_proj.weight.dtype)
```

For a quantized layer the stored weight is not in the activation dtype (FP8 is `float8_e4m3fn`). The bf16
activations are cast to FP8 with no scale before `qkv_proj` and `gate_up_proj`, and the FP8 linear method then
receives an FP8 input with `input_scale=None`. Block-wise and per-tensor FP8 Qwen2/Qwen3 dense models fail during
decode graph capture:

```python
import sglang as sgl
sgl.Engine(model_path="Qwen/Qwen3-4B", quantization="fp8")
# AssertionError: assert input_scale is not None ...   (fp8_utils.apply_fp8_linear)
sgl.Engine(model_path="Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8")              # block-wise FP8, ROCm gfx950
# [AITER] quant_kernels.cu:795 dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant_kernel not implemented for dtype fp8
# Fatal Python error: Aborted
```

MXFP8 does not crash, because the gfx950 MXFP8 GEMM re-quantizes its input. But every activation first goes
through a scale-1 E4M3 cast. In a 3-step miles GRPO A/B with unified MXFP8 (Qwen3-4B, 2x MI350X, same seeds, only
`qwen2.py`/`qwen3.py` differing), the mean train/rollout log-prob abs diff is 0.054 without this change and 0.037
with it.

`main` is not affected: it still casts with `.bfloat16()`.

## Change

Compare and cast against the projection's `params_dtype`, the model's activation dtype, which is what the
true-on-policy cast is meant to restore. For unquantized layers `params_dtype == weight.dtype`, so nothing
changes. The dtype is captured in `__init__` because the LoRA wrapper that later replaces `qkv_proj` /
`gate_up_proj` does not expose `params_dtype`.

Happy to have this folded into `[1/42]` at the next rebase instead.

## Testing

`sglang-miles` at 92fec6958d vs this branch, MI350X, TP1, `sgl.Engine(..., mem_fraction_static=0.6)`, greedy,
4 prompts x 64 new tokens. The ROCm image's sgl-kernel predates the fp32 rotary cache, so both trees cast
`cos_sin_cache` to the query dtype on HIP to run:

| Model / args | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8` | aborts in graph capture | ok |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`, `quantization="fp8"` | AssertionError in graph capture | ok |
| `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `quantization="fp8"` | AssertionError in graph capture | ok |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-4B` | ok | identical output |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`, `true_on_policy_contract="qwen3_dense_true_on_policy_v1"`, `rl_on_policy_target="fsdp"`, `attention_backend="triton"` | ok | identical output |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`, `enable_lora=True`, `max_lora_rank=16`, `lora_target_modules=["qkv_proj","o_proj","gate_up_proj","down_proj"]` | ok | identical output |
| MXFP8 Qwen3-4B | ok | ok (outputs change, see above) |

On an Oct 14 `sglang-miles` build with the same two-file change, GSM8K (250 test questions, greedy, 768 new
tokens): BF16 92.0% -> 92.0%, block FP8 aborts -> 92.4%, MXFP8 92.4% -> 92.4%.

Not run on CUDA. The `quantization="fp8"` assertion is in platform-independent code.

issues.title: [SM120] Enable FlashInfer GDN prefill default for consumer Blackwell
issues.body:
## Motivation

`flashinfer_gdn_prefill_default()` returns `None` on SM120, so consumer/workstation
Blackwell runs GDN prefill on Triton by default — even though `gdn_flashinfer.py` already
has an SM120-specific prefill path (`use_state_pool = sm_major >= 10`,
`_prefill_needs_fp32_state = sm_major >= 12`). This PR adds SM120 to that default-selection
policy as its own validated bucket, and adds unit coverage for the bucket's boundaries.

## Modifications

**1. SM120 gets its own row in `flashinfer_gdn_prefill_default()`** — admitted to the
capability check (`sm_major not in (9, 10)` → `(9, 10, 12)`), then given SM100's runtime
envelope with its own state dtype:

| arch | CUDA floor | max `chunked_prefill_size` | expected state dtype |
|------|-----------|----------------------------|----------------------|
| SM90  | none  | 32768 | fp32 |
| SM100 | >= 13 | 8192  | bf16 |
| **SM120** (new) | **>= 13** | **8192** | **fp32** |

* **fp32 state** — the SM120 kernel entry requires it. On a bf16 pool the clean tree raises
  `RuntimeError: initial_state must have dtype torch.float32, got torch.bfloat16` from
  `delta_rule_cp_sm120.py`, which is exactly what `_prefill_needs_fp32_state` converts
  around. fp32 is also what `mamba_ssm_dtype` resolves to by default, so the widening takes
  effect on the default path.
* **CUDA >= 13, chunk <= 8192** — SM120 goes through `use_state_pool`, i.e. the same chunked
  state-pool path SM100 is gated on, so it inherits the same envelope rather than SM90's
  looser one.

SM90 and SM100 behaviour is byte-identical to `main`.

**2. Unit coverage** in `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_gdn_prefill_backend_policy.py`:
grant case for SM120 + fp32 + CUDA 13; rejection cases for `sm120_bf16_state`,
`sm120_cuda_12`, `sm120_large_chunk` (8193), plus `sm90_bf16_state` / `sm100_fp32_state` so
the "one validated dtype per major" rule is explicit. The two boundary rows are
load-bearing: with the looser first-commit gate they fail with
`AssertionError: 'flashinfer' is not None`.

## Accuracy Test

1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 72GB Blackwell (SM120), CUDA 13.0, TP1,
`RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` (hybrid GDN), `--chunked-prefill-size 8192
--disable-radix-cache`.

* **Default fires** — with no explicit flag the dispatcher logs
  `decode=TritonGDNKernel, extend=FlashInferGDNKernel, verify=TritonGDNKernel`
  (and since the gate passed, the pool was fp32).
* **Determinism** — greedy decoding (`temperature=0`) is byte-identical across two runs.
* **Long request** — 2359-token prompt completes coherently.
* **Multi-chunk / packed-sequence stress** — `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`,
  in 4000 / out 200, `--random-range-ratio 1.0 --seed 42`, C=32, N=48:
  **48/48 succeeded, zero failures**, 9600 = 48x200 output tokens.
  Server counters confirm both hunks were exercised: `#new-token == 8192` (full chunk) 22
  times, and `#new-seq` up to 6, so the multi-sequence `cu_seqlens` packing path is covered
  too, not only the single-sequence one.

## Benchmark and Profiling

Prefill A/B, same binary and request stream, measured **server-side on back-to-back full
blocks only** (`#new-token == 8192`), n=22 per arm over matched 11 s windows:

```
                min      median      max       (tok/s, #new-token == 8192)
FlashInfer     32969     34511     37186   ████████████████████
Triton         29779     31764     33635   ██████████████████
```

* median 34511 / 31764 = **+8.7%**
* pairwise rank statistic: FlashInfer > Triton in **483 of 484** (22x22) pairs; FlashInfer
  exceeds Triton's *max* in 21/22 and Triton falls below FlashInfer's *min* in 21/22 — the
  distributions are near-disjoint, far outside the 0.4-0.8% cross-restart variance on this
  box.

This is an **end-to-end prefill forward** delta, not a per-kernel profile.

Two disclosures so reviewers don't have to dig them out:

1. **The A/B ran on a bf16 pool.** Both arms were driven by explicit
   `--linear-attn-prefill-backend {flashinfer,triton}` — which bypasses the policy under
   change — with `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`. So it isolates exactly the prefill backend
   this PR defaults, but on the pool dtype this PR's gate *rejects*. On the fp32 pool the PR
   enables, the kernel receives the same fp32 initial state (the
   `_prefill_needs_fp32_state` conversion becomes a no-op) and only state marshalling
   differs — but I have not measured that arm beyond the accuracy checks above, and I am not
   translating +8.7% into a claim about it. Happy to re-run the A/B on the default fp32 path
   if you want the numbers on-configuration.
2. **One-time first-touch cost.** Client-side median TTFT reads *worse* on the FlashInfer
   arm (5578.89 vs 2018.90 ms). That is a single batch: the first time a 4224-token prefill
   shape is seen it runs at **979.79** vs Triton's **28290.28** tok/s (4.31 s vs 0.149 s),
   and that ~4.16 s accounts for essentially the whole 3.80 s duration difference.
   Steady-state decode is untouched, as expected for a prefill-only flag (`mean_tpot` 21.67
   vs 21.74 ms, +0.3%).

Scope actually validated: **bf16 pool + chunk 8192 + TP1** for the throughput A/B, fp32 pool
for the default-path accuracy checks. Not covered: TP>1 on SM120, chunk sizes other than
8192, `enable_dynamic_chunking`.

## Notes for reviewers

* **Prefill and decode stay mutually exclusive on SM120.** `server_args.py` raises when
  `linear_attn_decode_backend == "flashinfer"` and `mamba_ssm_dtype != "bfloat16"` on
  capability >= 10. Since this gate requires fp32, the two cannot both be on for SM120:
  fp32 → FlashInfer prefill + Triton decode; bf16 → FlashInfer decode possible, prefill
  stays Triton. Pre-existing, not addressed here; flagging it because fp32 also doubles SSM
  state bytes vs bf16, which matters on capacity-bound deployments.
* **MTP/target-verify untouched** — `supports_target_verify = sm_major in (9, 10)` excludes
  SM120, confirmed by `verify=TritonGDNKernel` in the log above.
* Fully opt-outable: `--linear-attn-prefill-backend triton`, and anything outside the
  envelope (CUDA 12, chunk > 8192, bf16 pool, page-major KV, dynamic chunking,
  deterministic inference) falls back to Triton automatically.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code according to `pre-commit` (black 26.1.0 / isort / ruff / codespell,
      clean locally).
- [x] Add unit tests — `test_gdn_prefill_backend_policy.py` + `test_linear_attn_config.py`
      pass locally (21 tests, 27 subtests). CI has not run them: the `pr-gate` jobs report
      `Missing required label 'run-ci'`, so a maintainer label is needed for them to go
      green here.
- [x] Update documentation — no user-facing doc change; the selection rules live in the
      function's own comment, which this PR rewrites to give the per-arch reason.

issues.title: [Fix] spec: Build DFlash draft layers under their checkpoint names and refuse tensors the draft would drop
issues.body:
## Motivation

A quantized DFlash draft is built from its quantization config by module name and loaded by tensor name, and the two did not see the same names. `DFlashDraftModel` gave every decoder layer an empty prefix unless the checkpoint was a Nemotron 3.5 draft, so quantization matching saw a bare `qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` for all layers. Name-based `ignore` entries such as `re:.*self_attn\.q_proj$` never applied, the attention projections were built as quantized layers, and `load_weights` then dropped the checkpoint's BF16 `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` tensors without a word because the fused module had no `.weight` to put them in. The packed weight went into attention uninitialized. With the W8A16 draft from the recipe below, built from the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, main hits a device-side assert (`srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` in `indexSelectSmallIndex`) on the server's own warm-up request, after a startup that only logged `DFLASH fused KV materialization disabled: quantized qkv_proj is not supported for this path`.

The second half of the same problem is `fc`: outside the Nemotron path it was a plain `nn.Linear`, so a checkpoint that quantizes `fc` (`fc.weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`, or FP8 `fc.weight` + `weight_scale_inv`) had those tensors dropped the same way and `fc` kept its random init, so the draft would propose from a random projection of the target's hidden states. Several of the quantized DFlash2 drafts published on the Hub for Qwen3.8-27B quantize `fc` as well.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py` only:

- A draft whose own checkpoint is quantized, meaning its `config.json` carries a `quantization_config`, builds every decoder layer with `layers.{i}` (or `{prefix}.layers.{i}`), as Nemotron drafts and drafts whose class sets `supports_quantization` (LiLiCorr, #42057) already do. A quantization config then matches the same names the checkpoint uses.
- `packed_modules_mapping` on the draft model class, which the loader already injects into the quant config, so an `ignore` list that names `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` or `gate_proj`/`up_proj` applies to the fused module. llm-compressor writes the shard names it was given, as in the recipe below. As for every other model with such a mapping, an ignore list that names a single shard now fails with the fused-layer scheme mismatch error instead of matching nothing.
- The same drafts build `fc` as a `ReplicatedLinear` with the quant config, as those drafts already do. Any other draft is built as on main, with empty layer prefixes and a dense `nn.Linear` `fc`. That includes an unquantized draft that inherits the target's `--quantization`: with `--quantization fp8` its other linears are already quantized online on main, and a quantizable `fc` would have become FP8 as well. The check reads `config.json` only, so a draft described only by `hf_quant_config.json` is also built as on main, and a quantized `fc` tensor in it is now refused, as described below, instead of being dropped.
- The `fc.weight` shape check keeps the packed-aware form and `encoder.fc.*` vendor names alias to `fc.*`. `load_weights` refuses a checkpoint that fills the decoder layers but never `fc`: a quantizable `fc` starts uninitialized, and a dense one left at its random init gave unusable drafts before as well. A projector-only load, as Domino does, is unaffected.
- `load_weights` refuses a checkpoint tensor whose module the draft has, under a parameter name that module does not have (a dense tensor for a packed layer, or a packed tensor for a dense layer, under the draft's own or the vendor `encoder.` name), with the module's actual parameter names in the message. Tensors for modules the draft does not have are still ignored, and so are the ones that have no draft parameter by design: `.bias`, the `.inv_freq` / `.cos_cached` / `.sin_cached` rotary caches, and the `.input_scale` / `.output_scale` / `.k_scale` / `.v_scale` / `.kv_scale` activation and KV-cache scales.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_quantized_draft_layout.py`: the layer names through the real decoder layer, the shard-only ignore list reaching the fused projection, `fc` quantized / ignored / dense, an unquantized draft under an inherited online FP8 config keeping main's names and dense `fc`, packed and dense `fc` loading (own and vendor name), the two refusals, and the tensors that must still be ignored. On main 8 of the 13 cases fail.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests (CPU): `test_dflash_quantized_draft_layout.py` 13 passed (8 fail on main); `test_dflash_logits.py`, `test_dflash_domino.py`, `test_oot_dflash_hooks.py`, `test_dflash_extra_buffer_lazy.py`, `test_dflash_overlap_hostsync.py`, `model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py` 51 passed. The branch is rebased onto 26a1377, after #42057, and these CPU tests were re-run there.

The quantized draft is built from the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` with llm-compressor's model-free PTQ: INT8 weight-only for the MLP, `o_proj` and `fc`, with q/k/v, the candidate selector and the convolution kernels left BF16:

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W8A16",
    scheme="W8A16",
    ignore=["re:.*self_attn\\.(q|k|v)_proj$", "re:.*candidate_selector.*",
            "re:.*kernel_projection$", "re:.*norm.*"],
)
```

issues.title: [Fix] lora: support PEFT rsLoRA and GDN adapters on Qwen3.5-family hybrid MoE
issues.body:
## Motivation

SGLang can't serve PEFT LoRA adapters that target the Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers of Qwen3.5-family hybrid models (for example `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` and `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`). There are three separate problems:

1. **rsLoRA scaling is ignored.** Adapters trained with `use_rslora=True` are applied at `alpha/r` instead of `alpha/sqrt(r)`. At rank 64 that makes them 8× too weak, and served outputs look close to the base model's.
2. **GDN projections aren't loaded.** The target allowlist omits PEFT's GDN names (`in_proj_qkv`, `in_proj_z`, `in_proj_a`, `in_proj_b`). PEFT's combined `in_proj_qkv`/`in_proj_z` tensors aren't packed into the runtime `in_proj_qkvz`, and there is no packed target for the gating projections.
3. **Shared-expert-only adapters wrap the routed experts.** An adapter that targets only the dense shared expert still has the routed-expert bank wrapped for LoRA and gets expert LoRA buffers, because both paths use `gate/up/down_proj` names. That allocates unused memory. It also rejects MoE runner backends without routed LoRA support (for example native NVFP4 `flashinfer_cutlass`), even though the adapter never touches the routed experts.

## Modifications

Three commits, each reviewable on its own:

- **`fix(lora): honor rank-stabilized adapter scaling`.** Use `alpha/sqrt(r)` when the PEFT config sets `use_rslora`; ordinary LoRA is unchanged.
- **`fix(lora): load PEFT GDN projections for Qwen3.5 hybrids`.**
  - Normalize and pack combined QKV/Z into `in_proj_qkvz`. PEFT's shared `lora_A` is repeated per Q/K/V rank block.
  - Pack B/A into a new `in_proj_ba` target, in the base layer's order.
  - Add the target names, stacked multipliers and dimensions.
  - Add a synthetic public-model reproducer, `test/manual/lora/repro_qwen35_peft_dense_adapters.py`.
- **`fix(lora): leave untargeted routed experts on the base backend`.**
  - Infer from the initial adapters' tensors whether routed-expert LoRA is needed. When it isn't, leave the routed `FusedMoE` modules unwrapped and skip their LoRA buffers.
  - Starting with no initial adapters keeps the previous behaviour, so dynamic MoE loading still works.
  - Loading routed-expert tensors later into a dense-only pool raises a clear error instead of failing silently.

This adds no quantization kernel and no routed-expert LoRA implementation. The shared expert stays on its dense LoRA path (`--disable-shared-experts-fusion`).

## Accuracy Tests

- **Packing:** unit tests check that packed GDN products equal the original PEFT products, for both QKV/Z and B/A.
- **Synthetic public adapter**, rank 8 and 620 factors, generated from the public config only by the reproducer:
  - On `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` (revision `1355db6a`) with TP=2, all three public prompts change their next-token logprobs against the base.
  - Both TP ranks match all 380 normalized live factors exactly to their expected tensor slices.
  - Dynamic load and unload work.
- **Trained adapter:** a rank-64 rsLoRA adapter trained with PEFT on synthetic data, on attention, GDN and the shared expert. We compared fact recall on 445 held-out questions per adapter, served against local PEFT inference:
  - bf16 (`Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`, TP=2): within ±0.007 for all three adapters tested.
  - NVFP4 with `flashinfer_cutlass` (TP=1 and TP=2, bf16 or fp8_e4m3 KV): 0.007 to 0.025 below local, consistent with quantization.
  - Without these patches, the same adapters can't be loaded, or they recall at base-model level.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. For dense-only adapters, routed experts now skip the LoRA wrapper and buffers, so they run on the unmodified base MoE backend. We haven't benchmarked speed.

## Reproduction

```bash
python test/manual/lora/repro_qwen35_peft_dense_adapters.py \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 --base-model nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --revision 1355db6a052410cfd62085d94b58866fd0f2c3c5 --output-dir /tmp/qwen-dense-lora

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 --revision 1355db6a052410cfd62085d94b58866fd0f2c3c5 \
  --served-model-name qwen --tp-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --enable-lora --lora-backend triton --lora-strict-loading --lora-paths dense-example=/tmp/qwen-dense-lora \
  --max-lora-rank 8 --max-loras-per-batch 2 --max-loaded-loras 2 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000

python test/manual/lora/repro_qwen35_peft_dense_adapters.py --output-dir /tmp/qwen-dense-lora \
  --check-only --already-loaded --check-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 --served-model qwen --adapter-name dense-example
```

The adapter is selected as `model=qwen:dense-example`. The random adapter shows the adapter is applied; it says nothing about task quality.

Validated on SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) with torch 2.14.1+cu130, transformers 5.19.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2 and sglang-kernel 0.4.10. GPU runs used the Python radix-tree backend, because the dev container lacked the source checkout's Rust extension.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Mooncake EP has a native Intel XPU implementation (kvcache-ai/Mooncake#4900). This PR lets SGLang use it for expert parallelism over the TP ranks of one node:

```bash
sglang serve --model-path <MODEL> --device xpu --tp 4 --ep-size 4 \
    --moe-a2a-backend mooncake --attention-backend intel_xpu
```

## Modifications

- `--deepep-mode auto` now resolves to `low_latency` for mooncake, and `normal` is rejected at startup. Mooncake only implements low latency, so both used to fail in the dispatcher.
- XPU: a masked-layout MoE runner in `DeepEPMoE` using sgl-kernel's grouped GEMM, writing its output into the received slab. The Mooncake dispatcher sends BF16, passes the top-k weights at dispatch, and keeps its all-ranks-active tensors alive for the receive hooks.
- XPU: multi-node, DP attention, TBO/SBO, elastic EP, speculative decoding and `--disable-attn-tp-gather` are rejected at startup, and MoE layers with options the runner does not apply (expert biases, gemm1/SwiGLU alpha and limits, router weights on the input) when the model is built. `chunked_prefill_size` and `max_running_requests` are capped to the dispatch's per-rank capacity.
- `SGLANG_MOONCAKE_EP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` moves into `Envs`, with the same default.
- Docs on the XPU platform page and in the env var reference; unit tests for the argument handling, the XPU runners and the active-ranks ring.

issues.title: [Feat] [AMD] Quark: Run Quark MXFP4 MoE as W4A16 via triton_kernels on RDNA (gfx1151)
issues.body:
## Motivation

Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints (e.g. `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4`) cannot run correctly on RDNA GPUs such as gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S / Strix Halo), which have neither FP4 hardware nor an AITER FP4 MoE kernel:

- Without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the server crashes after weight loading with `NameError: name 'e8m0_shuffle' is not defined`, because `process_weights_after_loading` calls `e8m0_shuffle` on every non-gfx1250 GPU while the import is gated on `_use_aiter`.
- With `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, the server starts, but the output is garbage (GSM8K 8%, chat echoes the question). The scales are preshuffled into the gfx950 `e8m0_shuffle` layout while the weights are not shuffled (`_is_shuffle_moe_mxfp4` is gfx95-only), and aiter's `fused_moe` falls back to its "2stage default" kernel on gfx1151.

`triton_kernels`' `matmul` can already upcast MXFP4 weights inside the kernel with bf16 activations, and it computes correctly on gfx1151, so this PR uses it as a W4A16 path for these GPUs.

## Modifications

All changes are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/quark/schemes/quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`:

- Add `_use_triton_w4a16`, enabled on HIP when the GPU is neither gfx95x nor gfx1250 (opt out with `SGLANG_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16=0`). gfx950 and gfx1250 keep their existing AITER paths unchanged.
- `create_weights`: don't apply AITER MoE padding when the W4A16 path is active.
- `create_moe_runner`: skip the AITER runner requirement on the W4A16 path.
- `process_weights_after_loading`: on the W4A16 path, swizzle the packed MXFP4 weights and e8m0 scales with the existing `_swizzle_mxfp4` helper, build `PrecisionConfig`s (`b_microblock_size=32`, fp32 output for w2), and drop the original loaded tensors. The AITER preshuffle (and the `e8m0_shuffle` call) is no longer reached on these GPUs.
- `apply_weights`: on the W4A16 path, build expert-major ragged routing from the standard `topk_ids` / `topk_weights` entirely on device (`argsort` + `scatter_add_`, no `bincount`, so it's CUDA-graph capturable). Then run gate_up `matmul` (gather) → `silu_and_mul` → down `matmul` (scatter + router weights), and reduce the scattered `num_tokens * top_k` rows over `top_k`.
- The path asserts a serialized MXFP4 checkpoint and `silu` activation, so unsupported configurations fail loudly instead of computing wrong results.

Activations stay in bf16 (W4A16) rather than being quantized to MXFP4 as on gfx950, so accuracy is at least as good as the W4A4 path.

## Accuracy Tests

Model `amd/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4` on 1x gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S, 96 GB VRAM carve-out), `--attention-backend triton --context-length 8192`, sglang at `172b1b4825` in the `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm724-gfx1151-20260923` image (ROCm 7.2.4, torch 2.9.1, triton 3.7.0). The file touched here is unchanged between that commit and current `main`. Reference: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` (BF16) on the same machine and flags.

| Model | Path | MGSM-en (100, chat, thinking off) | GSM8K 5-shot (200) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B BF16 | unquantized | 0.98 | 0.945 |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | before, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` | — | 0.080 (50 q) |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | before, default | crash (`NameError: e8m0_shuffle`) | — |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-MXFP4 | **this PR** | **0.97** | **0.970** |

Kernel-level check on real layer-3 weights: the W4A16 MoE output vs. an fp32 reference built from the dequantized MXFP4 weights (`_dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16`) gives a relative error of 0.41–0.43% for m = 1 … 256 tokens.

issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] bugfix: Wan2.2 crash due to Triton kernel compilation
issues.body: ## Summary On gfx1250 with the Triton that ships in the ROCm SDK, `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` silently computed `x * scale + shift` instead of `x * (1 + scale) + shift`, dropping the identity term from adaLN modulation in every DiT block of every diffusion step. Output was wrong but plausible-looking — no crash, no warning. This gates the affected modulation math to fp32 on gfx1250 only. All other targets keep byte-identical codegen. ## Root cause The bug is in Triton's instruction encoding, not in SGLang. gfx1250 is the only target where Triton lowers bf16 elementwise math to packed `v_pk_*_bf16`; every other target promotes to fp32 first. Comparing the two Triton builds for `bf16 + 1.0`: ``` upstream 76940ad3 (fixed): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel:[0,1] ROCm SDK 4cff872c (broken): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel_hi:[1,0] ``` The inline constant `1.0` is the **fp32** pattern `0x3F800000`. Its high half `0x3F80` is bf16 `1.0`; its low half is `0x0000`. The SDK build selects the low half for `src1` in both lanes, so the addend is bf16 zero and the operation becomes a no-op. This affects `+`, `-` and `*` against any AMDGPU hardware inline float constant — `±0.5, ±1.0, ±2.0, ±4.0` — and nothing else. Ordinary literals (`1.5`, `100.0`) are encoded as a packed bf16 pair and are correct; tensor operands are correct. In this kernel `scale_constant` is exactly `1.0`, so it hit the broken case. The bug is fixed in upstream Triton, and `3865efc` (`[AMD] support gfx1250 on ROCM 10`) already moved the gfx1250 image onto a build that carries the fix (`BUILD_TRITON=1`, `TRITON_COMMIT=76940ad3`). This change keeps SGLang correct on the SDK Triton as well, so correctness no longer depends on which Triton the image happens to ship. ## Why fp32 and not `tl.full` `tl.full` looks like it should keep the constant out of the immediate, but it does not — LLVM folds the splat straight back in. Measured on the broken build: | form | result | emitted ISA | |---|---|---| | `scale_constant + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | `tl.full(...) + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | fp32 promote | **correct** | no packed bf16 immediate | fp32 promotion was the only form that produced clean ISA. It also keeps a single rounding on store, matching what the layernorm scale/shift kernels in this same file already do. ## Scope Gated behind `is_gfx1250_supported()` and passed as a `tl.constexpr`, so Triton resolves the branch at compile time — no runtime branch, and the `else` arm is the original code verbatim. NVIDIA, XPU, gfx942 and gfx950 compile to exactly what they did before, including the `tl.full` splat, so their numerics stay bit-identical. `is_gfx1250_supported()` is `lru_cache`d and returns `False` on non-HIP builds without touching CUDA. The kernel is shared by 11 DiT families, so this is not Wan-only: `wanvideo`, `causal_wanvideo`, `hunyuanvideo`, `hunyuan3d`, `qwen_image`, `glm_image`, `joy_image`, `helios`, `lingbot_world`, `longlive2`, `mova_video_dit`. They reach it through `LayerNormScaleShift` / `RMSNormScaleShift` / `ScaleResidualRMSNormScaleShift` with the default `scale_constant=1.0`. The VAE is unaffected — adaLN is a transformer construct, and an ISA scan over a full Wan2.2 run (1307 kernels, 118 using packed bf16) found this kernel as the only affected one. ## Testing After this PR is applied, the video can be played. Extracted pic comparison as below: Tested on rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi45x-test-triton4cff872c-20260923. Existing unit test `test_scale_shift_4d_matches_torch`, run against both Triton builds: | Configuration | Result | |---|---| | ROCm SDK Triton (broken), with fix | 16 passed | | Upstream Triton (fixed), with fix | 16 passed — no regression | | ROCm SDK Triton, fix reverted | **3 failed** (the bf16 + `scale_constant=1` cases) | | ROCm SDK Triton, gate forced off | **3 failed** — confirms the `else` arm is the original path | End-to-end Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on the broken SDK Triton (720×1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42) completed cleanly and matches a known-good baseline generated on the fixed Triton: correlation **0.991**, PSNR **29.3 dB**, mean abs diff 4.3/255. A dropped identity term collapses structure, so this margin is rounding and sampling non-determinism, not lost conditioning. Performance is unchanged. `bench_scale_shift_4d.py`, 3 runs each way, medians: 117.7 vs 119.9 µs (wan), 16.23 vs 16.24 µs (longlive). Within-group spread was ±20% on the larger workloads, so those deltas are noise — the kernel reads three tensors and writes one with no reuse, so it is bandwidth-bound and the extra `v_cvt` ops hide behind memory latency. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. issues.title: [Fix] spec: Let NEXTN and the DFlash2 selector reuse a packed target lm_head
issues.body:
## Motivation

A compressed-tensors checkpoint that quantizes `lm_head` in the pack-quantized INT format stores the head as `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`; the module has no `.weight`. The target serves fine on its own, but both speculative paths that borrow the target head refuse it:

- `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` dies at startup in `get_embed_and_head`: `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'`.
- `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` with a DFlash2 draft dies on the server's own warm-up request, so the server never becomes ready: `DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head or a supported lm_head.quant_method.`

Both come from `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` refusing any head without `.weight`. That check arrived with #27906 to keep the ModelOpt `lm_head.weight.dtype` reads safe. A packed head is exactly the case where `quant_method.apply` is the only way to get logits, and the target's own `LogitsProcessor` already does that through its trailing fallback branch. #35496 added the quant-method path to the DFlash2 selector, but the gate never let a packed head reach it. GGUF heads (`qweight`, no `.weight`) sit in the same position.

Reproduced on main (525f140) with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` quantized by llm-compressor so that `lm_head` is pack-quantized; the recipe is under Accuracy Tests. The branch is now rebased onto 9039662; #39643 rewrote `init_lm_head` in the spec workers along the way. The CPU tests were re-run on 9039662, and the GPU runs below are from 525f140.

## Modifications

- `layers/logits_processor.py`: `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` no longer requires `.weight`. Only the three ModelOpt methods, whose branches read `lm_head.weight.dtype`, are refused when the tensor is missing. In `_compute_lm_head` a head without a dense weight now takes the `quant_method.apply` branch and keeps the fp32 activation cast the old fallback gave it under `--enable-fp32-lm-head` (that flag with a marlin-packed head was and stays unsupported); the old trailing fallback becomes an explicit error, since every head that used to reach it is now admitted by the gate. Only the second, bound definition of the gate is changed; #39707 removes the shadowed first copy.
- `models/qwen3_5.py`, `models/qwen3_5_text.py`: `get_embed_and_head` hands out `None` for a packed head instead of reading `.weight`. `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` then shares the whole module through `set_lm_head_from_target`, which `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` already implements.
- `speculative/spec_utils.py`: `lm_head_is_packed` (no `.weight`, and not a `PPMissingLayer`). `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`: when the target head is packed and the draft cannot take the module (no `set_lm_head_from_target`, or a hot-token map), fail with a clear error instead of decoding with the draft's own head. Since #39643 a pipeline stage runs the same `init_lm_head`, so under PP a packed head is shared as a module too; I have not run PP, which needs two GPUs.
- Out of scope: `dspark_draft_sampler.py`, `deepseek_v4_dspark.py` and `domino_utils.py` still read `lm_head.weight` and keep failing on a packed head as before. DSpark's `project_through_lm_head` goes through the gate and is fixed along the way.
- `speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`: it shares the head tensor only, so it fails with a clear error on a packed target, before loading anything, instead of handing the draft `head=None`. Frozen-KV MTP is left alone: its only draft, Gemma 4, keeps its own `lm_head`. `qwen3_5_text.set_embed_and_head` accepts `None` for either half, matching what its accessor can now return.
- Tests: the two DFlash2 selector cases in `test_dflash_logits.py` are parametrized over a head that keeps packed bytes under `.weight` and one that has no `.weight` at all. New CPU file `test_spec_packed_target_lm_head.py` covers the gate (admission, and refusal of each ModelOpt method without a dense weight), the fp32 cast, the error path, the three accessors, and `init_lm_head` sharing the module, refusing when it cannot, and still accepting a pipeline stage without a head. On main 8 of the 22 cases fail; the rest pin behaviour that must not change.

## Accuracy Tests

Checkpoints, both built from the official weights with llm-compressor's model-free PTQ. The target has a W4A16 body and a W8A16 `lm_head`, both pack-quantized; the in-checkpoint MTP layer stays BF16:

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationConfig, QuantizationScheme
from compressed_tensors.quantization.quant_scheme import W4A16, W8A16
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-lm_head-W8A16",
    config=QuantizationConfig(config_groups={
        "lm_head": QuantizationScheme(targets=["re:.*lm_head$"], **W8A16),  # first match wins
        "body": QuantizationScheme(targets=["Linear"], **W4A16),
    }),
    ignore=["re:.*visual.*", "re:.*mtp.*", "re:.*in_proj_(a|b)$", "re:.*conv1d.*",
            "re:.*norm.*", "re:.*embed_tokens.*"],
)
```

The reference is the same call without the `lm_head` group and with `"lm_head"` added to `ignore`, so its head stays BF16. DFLASH uses the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` draft.

One RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB, TP=1), `--disable-overlap-schedule`. NEXTN: steps 3, top-k 1, draft tokens 4. DFLASH: block size 8. Accuracy is SGLang's own GSM8K eval, one request at a time so completions can be compared across runs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 1 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512
```

| target `lm_head` | branch | spec | result | GSM8K (200) | accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | main | none | serves | 0.960 | |
| BF16 | main | NEXTN | serves | 0.970 | 3.629 |
| BF16 | main | DFLASH | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| W8A16 packed | main | none | serves | 0.965 | |
| W8A16 packed | main | NEXTN | `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'` at startup | | |
| W8A16 packed | main | DFLASH | `RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense ...` on the server's warm-up request | | |
| W8A16 packed | this PR | NEXTN | serves | 0.965 | 3.629 |
| W8A16 packed | this PR | DFLASH | serves; the selector is folded into the draft CUDA graph | 0.970 | 6.035 |

Accept length is the mean of the scheduler's `accept len` over every decode-log window of the run, bonus token included. The `sglang:spec_accept_length` gauge only holds the last window, so it is not used here.

Speculative decoding matches non-speculative decoding only up to numerics, so completions are compared against the same checkpoint without speculation. With the packed head, 172/200 NEXTN and 167/200 DFLASH completions match the packed-head target decoding on its own. On main, the BF16-head target matches its own non-speculative run in 167/200 (NEXTN) and 166/200 (DFLASH) completions.

Unit tests (CPU): `test_spec_packed_target_lm_head.py` + `test_dflash_logits.py` 22 passed (8 fail on main); `test_eagle_draft_extend_logits.py`, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath.py`, `models/test_qwen3_5_packed_weight_loader.py`, `models/test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4.py` 31 passed; the `lm_head_guard` cases of `model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py` 4 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for dense or ModelOpt heads: the gate returns what it returned before and the same kernel runs. A packed head goes from refusing to start to serving; the draft calls the same `quant_method.apply` the target already runs for its own logits. I have no clean timing for it yet, since the GPU these runs used was shared with other jobs.

issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** |

The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS.

## Modifications

- Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**.
- The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change.
- Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check.
- The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layout and values; short sequences keep the zero-copy view; long sequences are dense only on HIP; the copy preserves every bit (`torch.equal` against the transposed view).
- End to end, the change only moves tensor layout, so no numerical change is expected by construction. Verified on Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 and 2048^2 with a fixed seed: identical image, no metric shift.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1, default environment, `torch_sdpa` backend, gfx1151. Seconds per denoising step (mean over all steps), two runs per arm:

| Shape | before | after | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024^2 / 20 steps | 3.8524 | 3.8523 | 1.00x |
| 2048^2 / 12 steps | 78.04 / 77.42 | 22.04 / 22.11 | **3.54x** |

Within-arm spread <1%. The 2048^2 gain is AOTriton flash instead of the generic kernel; the 1024^2 row confirms the threshold leaves short sequences untouched.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit (`isort` + `ruff` pass).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations (no user-facing docs describe this backend detail).

## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a
**non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 that view costs AOTriton a lot: the same
`attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens,
versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves
throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the
same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost.

## What this adds

* `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a
  non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no
  masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of
  K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K
  pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4
  warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax
  keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA,
  `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores).
* A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`
  (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`,
  `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything
  else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are
  materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens
  those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on
  SDPA.

## Numbers (Ryzen AI MAX 395, gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=128 bf16)

Same dense head-major operands for both, kernel-only (median of 10, 3 warmups):

| seq | AOTriton SDPA | Triton | speedup | Triton TF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16.4 ms | 9.7 ms | 1.70x | 28.5 |
| 16384 | 239.3 ms | 138.5 ms | 1.73x | 31.8 |

The 16384 row uses the shipped one-stage pipeline; the 4096 row predates the
stage sweep and is unaffected by it.

What the flag actually changes end to end, i.e. including the layout
materialisation the kernel needs versus the strided call the backend makes today:

| seq | today (SDPA on the view) | with this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 22.2 ms | 16.6 ms | 1.34x |
| 8192 | 163.6 ms | 54.3 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2131 ms | 183.3 ms | 11.6x |

The 16K row is the interesting one: AOTriton's strided-operand regression grows
faster than the work does, so at 128 head dim the gap widens with sequence
length. Diffusion DiT self-attention at 2048x2048 sits exactly there.

## Kernel resources and scaling

Compiled at S=16384 the kernel uses 256 VGPR per lane (the RDNA3 limit) with
**zero spills** and 16 KiB of LDS, which keeps four CTAs resident per CU. A
second pipeline stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency, and measured
146.3 ms instead of 138.5 ms — that is why the shipped configuration uses one
stage. Of 81 swept `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x warps x stages` points, 66 compiled and
this one ranked first; `BLOCK_M = 128` with 2-4 warps spills 350-1149 registers
and drops to 3.8-6.7 TF.

Sweeping the sequence length shows where the materialisation stops paying:

| seq | SDPA on the view | this PR | speedup | kernel vs dense AOTriton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.37 ms | 2.10 ms | 0.65x | 1.81x |
| 2048 | 5.39 ms | 5.58 ms | 0.97x | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 21.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 1.29x | 1.70x |
| 8192 | 150.2 ms | 54.2 ms | 2.77x | 1.62x |
| 16384 | 2180.5 ms | 182.4 ms | 11.95x | 1.64x |
| 32768 | 12932.8 ms | 658.6 ms | 19.64x | 1.65x |

The kernel alone wins at every length (1.62-1.81x against dense AOTriton, and
2.1x to 22x against the strided view); what crosses over is the three
materialisations, which are 69% of the call at 1024 tokens and 20% at 16384.
Hence the 4096-token floor.

Numerics against an fp32 reference: max abs diff 1.1e-3, mean 1.9e-5, no element
above 0.05 (bf16 rounding on both sides).

## Tests

* `test/registered/unit/attention/test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` (CPU, no GPU
  needed; the kernel is mocked): env gate, non-ROCm, torch.compile, causal,
  dropout, fp32, `head_dim != 128`, `seq % 64`, short sequences (`seq < 4096`),
  mismatched lengths, kernel refusal → SDPA fallback; operand strides and `scale`
  forwarded to the kernel. `10 passed`.
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` (AMD CI):
  fp32-reference numerics at 128/256/512 tokens, zero-padded K/V with `kv_pad`,
  predicate rejections. `4 passed` on gfx1151.

Both were run on gfx1151 with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at a patched copy of the
installed package, so they are not compile-only checks.

## Relation to other work

* #46065 materialises dense SDPA operands; that closes the "strided view" half of
  the gap (AOTriton back to 240 ms at 16K) but not the remaining 1.63x.
* Model-side qkv changes and sparse-attention kernels are out of scope here.

## Caveats

- The default is off: only gfx1151 has been measured. gfx11 should behave the
  same, gfx9x untested — flip the default once there are numbers.
- Sequences below 4096 tokens deliberately stay on SDPA. The floor is the
  measured crossover from the table above, not a derived bound: the kernel alone
  is faster at every length, but the three head-major materialisations dominate
  short calls and make the full path a net loss there.
- End-to-end diffusion (Qwen-Image 2.1 at 2048x2048) throughput is not measured
  in this PR; the benchmark above is operator-level.

issues.title: [Qwen3.5] Fuse gated RMSNorm and FP8 quantization
issues.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5 Gated DeltaNet normalizes each local value-head row at width 128 and immediately feeds the flattened result into an output projection that dynamically quantizes activations in the same 128-wide groups.

The existing path materializes BF16 output from gated RMSNorm, then reads it again in a separate FP8 quantization kernel. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 has 30 affected Gated DeltaNet layers, making this a repeated launch and memory round-trip in every target forward.

This PR fuses those operations while preserving the baseline BF16 rounding boundary.

## Modifications

- Add a Triton gated RMSNorm + group-128 FP8 quantization kernel.
- Support both FP32 scales and Blackwell's packed UE8M0 TMA-aligned scale layout.
- Validate and consume prequantized `(fp8, scale)` input in the DeepGEMM block-FP8 path.
- Enable the fusion only for the compatible CUDA/Qwen/DeepGEMM/BF16/block-128 path.
- Add `SGLANG_DISABLE_QWEN_GDN_NORM_QUANT_FUSION` as an A/B opt-out.
- Classify speculative target verification and draft extension as decode work in stage-based profiling. This is measurement support and is excluded from performance attribution.
- Add unit tests for stage classification and DeepGEMM prequantized input, plus B200 kernel equivalence tests.

## Accuracy Tests

Full GSM8K with real MTP, simulated acceptance disabled, 1,319 examples, TP=2 on 2×B200:

| Variant | Accuracy | Stop rate | Length-truncated | Errors |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fusion disabled | 96.44% | 99.39% | 0.61% | 0% |
| Fusion enabled | 96.44% | 99.77% | 0.23% | 0% |

The official metrics matched an independent recount of all prediction rows: baseline had 1,311 `stop` and 8 `length` finishes; the candidate had 1,316 `stop` and 3 `length` finishes.

Focused tests on B200:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/test_profile_stage.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_deepgemm_prequant.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_rms_norm_gated_fp8_quant.py
```

Result: `15 passed, 8 subtests passed in 27.60s`.

Kernel coverage includes 1/4/8/16/257/16,384 logical tokens and both FP32 and packed UE8M0 scales. UE8M0 scales are bit-identical. Quantized data is bit-identical through 16 tokens; at the two larger shapes, only 1 and 2 values differ by one adjacent FP8 code out of 526,336 and 33,554,432 values.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` at revision `95a723d08a9490559dae23d0cff1d9466213d989`  
Hardware: 2×B200, TP=2  
Workload: static batch, 60,000 input tokens, 2,000 output tokens, five repetitions, radix cache disabled  
MTP matrix: NEXTN, 3 speculative steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens, simulated acceptance length 3

### Decode throughput

| Mode | BS | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MTP | 1 | 644.772 | 651.186 | +1.00% |
| MTP | 4 | 2,102.866 | 2,132.570 | +1.41% |
| MTP | 8 | 3,475.598 | 3,494.970 | +0.56% |
| MTP | 16 | 5,381.488 | 5,442.692 | +1.14% |
| non-MTP | 1 | 325.580 | 330.924 | +1.64% |
| non-MTP | 4 | 1,092.584 | 1,104.976 | +1.13% |
| non-MTP | 8 | 1,803.088 | 1,820.238 | +0.95% |
| non-MTP | 16 | 2,841.962 | 2,863.986 | +0.78% |

Candidate decode CV was at most 0.091%, and MTP acceptance length remained 3.0 in every matrix repetition. No required decode point regressed. MTP BS1 total-latency mean was affected by one prefill outlier; median total latency improved by 0.77%.

Representative MTP and non-MTP traces at BS1 and BS16 show:

- 30 fewer kernel launches per target decode step;
- the old gated RMSNorm kernel disappears;
- the fused kernel appears once per GDN layer;
- the corresponding standalone quantization count falls by 30;
- the affected norm/quant kernel family takes 15.5%–19.2% less GPU time.

The CUDA-graph norm-plus-quant microbenchmark improves by 7.2%–20.3% across the tested token shapes.

Validation also passed `py_compile`, changed-file pre-commit, post-commit pre-commit, and `git diff --check`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused unit and kernel tests.
- [x] Documentation is not required because this does not change a user-facing API or default configuration contract.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
